_note: The single place that decides what leaves this computer for the shared store. Read by tools/index/supabase_sync.py. Order: (1) the never list blocks a path outright; (2) the first matching rule gives scope and module; (3) area_rules are the fallback by the index's area column; (4) anything still unmatched stays local. A rule with scope null keeps that path local. Paths are relative to the brain's root, prefixes are case-sensitive, never-list name patterns are case-insensitive.
_owner_confirmed_private_scopes_note: Set this to true only after the owner has answered, in writing, the question 'who can open the store's project in the provider's dashboard?' with 'only me'. While false, supabase_sync.py refuses to upload the scopes listed in private_scopes, whatever the command line says. Set it back to false the day anyone else gets dashboard or organisation access.
_client_scopes_allowed_note: Even with the flag true, a client:<slug> scope is uploaded only if its slug is listed here: the owner says yes per client. A client under a confidentiality agreement or with special-category data is never listed.

never._note: Blocks a path from every upload: no document row, no chunk, no record, no edge. Checked before any rule.
never._path_contains_note: Case-insensitive substring of the whole path. Add the folder of any prospect or client whose material is under a confidentiality agreement.
never._path_segments_note: A folder anywhere in the path whose name equals one of these (case-insensitive).
never._prefix_name_patterns_note: One entry per guarded client folder, e.g. {"prefix": "01_Clients/<slug>/", "name_contains": ["health", "medical", "patient", "pseudonym"]}: inside that folder a file whose name contains any of the words never goes up.
never._name_patterns_note: Case-insensitive glob on the file name. No file bytes ever go up; this list also keeps the names and digests of such files out.

_never_text_terms_note: A chunk or record whose text contains one of these terms (case-insensitive) is dropped, not redacted. Use it for the name of a party whose material is under a confidentiality agreement.

content._note: No file bytes go up, only meaningful data. Every file gets a metadata-only document row; chunk text comes only from text files (notes, registers, digests, mail renditions). A PDF, Office file, image or scan has no chunks of its own: its text travels as its sibling <name>.digest.md document. Raw extracted renditions (<name>.pdf.txt and the like) carry no chunks.

rules._note: leads, offers and their values stay local; give this a scope only when the team should search them
client root files (profile, status), e-mail indexes

area_rules._note: also the fallback for every finance-<entity code> area

record_kind_scopes._note: Records of these kinds are money and go to finance whatever their source file.
